settings.name_in_paper: Batched two-arm (and K-arm contextual) bandit data for inference on the margin
settings.out_of_scope_reason: The paper studies asymptotic statistical inference (asymptotic normality of OLS / Batched OLS estimators) on data collected by bandit algorithms; it gives no regret, sample-complexity or error-probability guarantees for a bandit learner.
unmapped: Objective is asymptotic inference (confidence intervals / hypothesis tests for the margin) as batch size n -> infinity with a fixed number of batches T
Noise: martingale-difference errors with conditional variance sigma^2 and bounded fourth moment
Non-stationary baseline rewards across batches (per-batch means beta_t)
settings.definition_quote: In each batch $t \in [1 \colon T]$, we select $n$ binary actions $\{ A_{t,i} \}_{i=1}^n \in \{0, 1\}^n$. We then observe independent rewards $\{ R_{t,i} \}_{i=1}^n$, one for each action selected.
